analyzed_vuln.description: `xmlRemoveID` performs a hash removal using `attr->id->value` and frees the ID entry via `xmlFreeIDTableEntry`, but then continues to access `attr->id` to clear fields (`attr->atype = 0; attr->id = NULL`). If the removed hash entry corresponds to the same `attr->id`, the callback frees that object, so `attr->id` is dangling during/after removal. This creates a use-after-free read at the `xmlHashRemoveEntry(..., attr->id->value, ...)` call path when the stale pointer is reused in re-entrant/freeing scenarios (as shown by ASan double invocation in same free path). Root cause is unsafe lifetime handling in `xmlRemoveID` (missing local copy / nulling before free / guard against repeated removal), not in the crash-site caller.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered in the `xml` fuzz harness via entity expansion and DTD-declared ID attributes that create an `xmlID` (`xmlAddIDSafe` from SAX attribute handling), then later free attribute nodes (`xmlFreeProp` -> `xmlRemoveID`) during parser cleanup of expanded entity content. Input must cause an attribute marked `XML_ATTRIBUTE_ID` with `attr->id` set, and a teardown path where ID removal is invoked on an attribute whose ID entry is removed/freed and then referenced again in the same logical cleanup flow, producing UAF.
